growth_story.headline: Palau's income per person rises and falls with its tourists: a 2016 peak, a pandemic collapse, and a rebound that has not yet regained the lost ground.
growth_story.arc: Palau's income per person has moved in three eras since 1990. From 1990 to 2000 it shrank by 0.8 percent a year on average, with deep falls in the early 1990s and again in 1999 and 2000, after the Asian crisis cut tourist visits. From 2001 to 2016 it grew 1.8 percent a year, carried by tourism and by building paid for with Compact grants from the United States; the global crisis cut it by 4.1 percent in 2008 and 4.7 percent in 2009, and a surge of visitors from China lifted it 8.2 percent in 2015 before the 2016 peak. Since 2017 it has shrunk by 0.2 percent a year on average: arrivals fell after the authorities limited charter flights, and pandemic border restrictions cut income per person by 6.0 percent in 2020 and 11.9 percent in 2021. Reopening, returning flights and new building brought rebounds of 12.2 percent in 2024 and 6.5 percent in 2025. Even so, income per person in 2025 was 3.5 percent below its 2016 peak and about where it first stood in 2015.

threads.title: Tourist boom and charter limits
threads.text: In 2015 a surge of tourists, mostly from China, lifted income per person 8.2 percent. The rush strained infrastructure and leaned towards low-budget visitors, so the authorities limited charter flights. Income per person fell 3.5 percent in 2017 as arrivals dropped.

threads.title: Pandemic and a slow reopening
threads.text: Pandemic border restrictions hit hard: income per person fell 6.0 percent in 2020 and 11.9 percent in 2021. Recovery was slow after the border fully reopened in July 2022, held back by a lack of flights, and visitor numbers climbed again once flights from Taipei, China and Macau resumed. Tourist arrivals and building work are now the main drivers of growth.

threads.title: Compact money from Washington
threads.text: Since independence in 1994, grants under the Compact of Free Association with the United States have paid for infrastructure, budget support and a trust fund. A renewed agreement signed in May 2023 came on better financial terms.

citations.quote: As part of a 50-year Compact of Free Association, the United States provided US$580 million in financial aid to Palau during 1994-2009

citations.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2023 Article IV Consultation with Palau

threads.title: The Asian crisis
threads.text: Tourism lost ground after the Asian crisis of 1997, and income per person fell 7.3 percent in 1999 and 4.0 percent in 2000. The sources opened do not explain the sharp falls of 1992 and 1993.

citations.title: Public Information Notice: IMF Concludes 2001 Article IV Consultation with the Republic of Palau
citations.quote: Tourist activity has not recovered since the Asian crisis

threads.title: Global financial crisis
threads.text: The global crisis hit Palau hard: income per person fell 4.1 percent in 2008 and 4.7 percent in 2009, and it did not pass its 2007 level again until 2014.

citations.title: Private Sector Assessment for Palau: Policies for Sustainable Growth Revisited
citations.quote: real gross domestic product (GDP) falling by a total of around 15% across FY2008–FY2009, as the economy was severely buffeted by the global financial crisis

since_last_year.text: The rebound carried on into 2025: income per person grew 6.5 percent after 12.2 percent in 2024. In January 2026 the IMF described the recovery as led by tourist arrivals and strong building work, with inflation falling back.

citations.title: IMF Executive Board Concludes 2025 Article IV Consultation with Republic of Palau
citations.quote: FY2025: growth estimated at 6.7 percent; inflation declined to 0.2 percent.

growth_story.tension: The IMF expects Palau's total output to pass its pre-pandemic level only in FY2026, yet income per person in the data was already back at its 2019 level in 2025. Income per person recovering faster than total output could mean fewer people sharing it, but none of the sources opened discuss population change.
